claims.text: A Pulumi package is the unit of versioning and distribution; components inside it inherit the package's version.
Pulumi recommends structuring Git repositories for publishing packages per the strategies in this guide, which improve reliability, maintainability, and delivery speed.
A source-based plugin package is distributed as source code in a Git repository, and its version is the Git tag on that repository.
Publishing a source-based package to the Pulumi IDP Private Registry is a two-step flow (apply a semver Git tag, run pulumi package publish), typically performed by a CI/CD pipeline that runs on tag.
`pulumi package publish` sends package metadata to Pulumi Cloud and places the package in the Private Registry.
Semver-tagged releases are only required for publishing to the Private Registry.
Source-based packages referenced directly from a Pulumi.yaml file can use any Git ref (tag, branch, or commit), regardless of whether it is a valid semantic version.

An executable-based plugin package is distributed as a pre-built plugin binary, typically alongside per-language SDKs published to package feeds (npm, PyPI, NuGet, Maven, Go module proxy, or private equivalents).
The version of an executable-based package is the version embedded in the published binary and SDKs.
Pulumi Cloud customers can additionally publish an executable-based package to the Private Registry via `pulumi package publish`.
A repository should contain exactly one Pulumi package, regardless of package type; multiple packages in one repository must release in lockstep or need custom per-package release tooling.
Multiple components inside a single package are fine and expected; they ship together at the package's version.
The Amazon EKS package in the Pulumi Registry bundles a managed Kubernetes cluster component along with supporting components needed to secure and operate it.
A single PulumiPlugin.yaml at the repository root defines the package, with components living alongside it.
Pulumi does not recommend using a single monorepo with one giant package for all components, because it forfeits meaningful semantic versioning.
When unrelated components share a package, every package release versions every component the same way, which violates semver.
Cross-references: links to Private Registry concept page, pulumi package publish CLI page, packaging-components anchors, and publishing-packages guide must exist.
